tasks.title: Choose the exam, stage and NICL stream
tasks.body:
# Choose the exam, stage and NICL stream

Start by selecting the target exam, then its Prelims or Mains stage. NICL also distinguishes Generalist and Information Technology streams. These choices determine the available paper blueprints and question pools; a familiar page layout does not mean every paper has the same structure.

Check the paper title, subjects, question count and timing before launching a simulation. Change the exam selection before building a practice set if you intend to prepare for a different examination. Attempts retain their exam and stream identity so the performance view can show the relevant history.

This guide describes the application's current configuration. It is not a new recruitment notification. Use the sourced exam notes and the relevant official notice when checking current eligibility, dates or rule changes; do not infer those from a previously saved mock attempt.

tasks.title: Browse the numbered mock-test series
tasks.body:
# Browse the numbered mock-test series

Open Tests after choosing the exam, stage and stream. Select the intended paper and browse the numbered test cards. The series uses visible cards and pagination rather than hiding the whole selection behind one edition dropdown.

A completed marker refers to a recorded attempt for that edition. It does not certify that a paper is an official previous-year booklet, and it does not mean another numbered simulation contains an entirely unrelated question family. The practice bank includes disclosed generated variants.

Preview the chosen test's paper information before starting. If a saved test is already active, resume or submit that attempt before launching another. This protects the answer sheet from being replaced by an accidental second start. Use custom practice for a shorter targeted set instead of treating a full-paper card as a topic quiz.

tasks.title: Understand section clocks and reload recovery
tasks.body:
# Understand section clocks and reload recovery

A timed simulation uses its saved start and section deadlines. Reloading a page does not grant a fresh time allowance. In a section-timed test, only the current allowed question IDs can be answered or navigated to; a visible future section label is not permission to enter it early.

Use the runner's displayed time remaining and section indicators. An inactive browser tab may delay visual updates, but that does not make elapsed wall-clock time disappear. When the clock has finished, the runner submits the current answer state.

Save and resume are recovery features, not a pause button for the simulated exam clock. If you want an interrupted, less formal session, choose a suitable custom practice setup before starting. Test configuration and recorded timestamps explain a restored attempt more reliably than the browser's last displayed counter.

tasks.title: Use answer clearing, review flags and submission
tasks.body:
# Use answer clearing, review flags and submission

Selecting an option records an answer for the current allowed question. Clearing the answer removes that selection; marking a question for review is a separate action. A review flag is a reminder, not a second answer or a guarantee that the question will remain accessible after its timed section ends.

Before submitting, compare answered and unanswered counts with the question navigation. Avoid assuming that simply visiting a question records a response. The runner protects submission against duplicate completion callbacks.

**Save & exit** first attempts to store the active sheet. If storage fails, the runner displays an error and keeps the test open instead of pretending that recovery is safe. Follow that message and submit or protect your data before clearing browser storage. Closing the tab without a successful save is not a reliable backup method.

tasks.title: Read objective scores and unanswered questions
tasks.body:
# Read objective scores and unanswered questions

The runner displays the configured marks for correct and wrong answers before you complete a paper. Those values belong to that quiz blueprint. Do not apply another exam's negative-marking assumption simply because both use multiple-choice questions.

The scoring engine records question reviews and section-level results alongside the attempt. Unanswered questions are distinct from wrong responses. A review flag does not itself change the mark calculation. Inspect the submitted review to understand which recorded answers contributed to the score.

Application scores describe a practice attempt, not an official result, selection probability or fabricated rank. When investigating an unexpected total, check the paper identity, configured marking values and answer sheet first. A manual paper without a matched key follows a different review path and must not be compared as though an official answer key had been verified.

tasks.title: Build a focused custom practice session
tasks.body:
# Build a focused custom practice session

Use Custom practice to choose subjects, a topic, difficulty, question count and time. This creates a targeted exercise rather than silently changing the pattern of a full-paper simulation. Check the available question pool after applying several filters; a very narrow combination can leave too few eligible items.

Start with a specific learning aim, such as revisiting a weak subject or working on a difficult topic. Change one or two settings deliberately so the later attempt is interpretable. A short custom set should not be mistaken for full coverage of an exam stage.

Saved-question and mistake sources further restrict the pool to your own recorded selections or history. If the pool is empty, broaden the filters or first build relevant history. The engine should report insufficient coverage rather than quietly filling a strict exam simulation with unrelated subjects.

tasks.title: Turn saved questions and mistakes into revision
tasks.body:
# Turn saved questions and mistakes into revision

Saving a question creates a deliberate revision collection. Mistake practice is built from recorded attempts. These are different sources: a saved question can be one you answered correctly, while a wrong answer does not necessarily mean you manually saved it.

Open Custom practice and select the intended source, then check the subject and difficulty filters. The displayed collection count and the current filtered pool can differ. Clear narrow filters before assuming that a saved item has disappeared.

Use the explanation after a session to identify why the response was wrong, then return to the linked learning material for the underlying topic. Repeating an already memorized option is weaker evidence of understanding than explaining the method. The app tracks the recorded attempt; it does not infer that a previously missed concept has been permanently mastered.

tasks.title: Check paper provenance before starting a PYQ
tasks.body:
# Check paper provenance before starting a PYQ

Read the archive's source and provenance labels before treating a PDF as an original booklet. Official scans, publisher reconstructions, memory-based papers and source indexes are different evidence types. A historical year alone does not establish official provenance.

Check whether the answer key is matched to that particular booklet. Without a matching key, the application may provide a timed answer sheet and manual review rather than inventing an objective score. A publisher reconstruction can also contain visible solutions in its source PDF.

Use full simulations in Tests when you want a closed-answer experience built from the editorial question bank. That bank is practice content, not a claim that its questions appeared in the historical exam. If a source link or key changes, update the provenance record and validator together instead of merely relabelling the paper as original.

tasks.title: Distinguish keyed paper attempts from manual review
tasks.body:
# Distinguish keyed paper attempts from manual review

The paper archive and the editorial test series use different content paths. In the archive, the PDF is the source artifact and the answer sheet is tied to that paper's metadata. Verify the year and booklet before entering answers.

A keyed attempt needs a validated match between the source paper and its answer key. Manual review is appropriate when that match is unavailable; it should not produce a convincing-looking automated score from guessed answers. Compare the archive's provenance notes with the attempt mode rather than assuming that every Start action has the same scoring support.

Keep your source PDF accessible when reviewing. Some reconstructions include their own solutions, which limits their usefulness as a closed-answer mock. If the goal is a clean timed simulation, use Tests and review its clearly labelled editorial status instead.

tasks.title: Use descriptive writing without losing drafts
tasks.body:
# Use descriptive writing without losing drafts

The writing desk is separate from objective scoring. Open the descriptive task for the relevant stage, read the prompt and work within the displayed practice time. An essay or precis draft is not automatically evaluated as an official qualifying result.

Writing drafts stay on the device and are scoped to the active account. A different signed-in candidate should not inherit another account's draft. Exporting general exam progress is not a reason to assume every active writing buffer has become a portable cloud document.

Before clearing site data or changing devices, preserve important writing elsewhere. Verify the account and selected task if an expected draft does not appear. Resume the appropriate draft rather than pasting an unrelated response over it. The application supports practice and continuity, while an actual examiner's marking process remains outside the app.

tasks.title: Separate account sync from device-only progress
tasks.body:
# Separate account sync from device-only progress

The app can hold progress locally, and configured deployments also support a signed-in cloud account. The current account owner matters: a local cache from one candidate must not be uploaded into another candidate's history just because both use the same browser.

During sign-in, the sync layer hydrates the account state before allowing ordinary uploads. Writes are serialized and guarded against stale account generations. If a network request finishes after an account switch, its old ownership must not be treated as current.

Read the visible sync status before relying on another device to contain the latest attempt. Keep a JSON export before recovery work or browser cleanup. Device-only use is useful for exploration, but it is not evidence of a completed cloud backup. Never place a Supabase service-role credential in browser configuration to work around an account error.

tasks.title: Export and restore both exam histories
tasks.body:
# Export and restore both exam histories

Open **Profile & backup** and choose **Export JSON** to keep a portable copy. The export includes the supported exam histories, attempts and saved questions. Keep the complete file instead of copying only the summary visible on screen.

To recover a saved export, choose **Import backup**, review its contents and confirm the intended replacement. Export the current destination state first if it contains progress you may still need. Import is a deliberate recovery action, not an automatic merge of every record from two histories.

Earlier Lakshya progress has a compatibility path, but a familiar filename does not prove that arbitrary JSON is valid. The import path validates the format and size. Active tests and writing drafts have their own device storage behavior, so preserve them separately before clearing data or moving to a new device.

tasks.title: Review performance in the correct exam context
tasks.body:
# Review performance in the correct exam context

Open Performance after completing attempts and select the relevant exam, stage and stream. Compare like-for-like sessions: a short easy practice set and a full timed simulation do not provide equivalent evidence simply because both show a percentage.

Use subject-level rows and the question review to distinguish accuracy, unanswered items and timing. A low total can have different causes, including knowledge gaps, deliberate skips or a section clock expiring. Read those causes before turning the result into a revision plan.

The mistake-practice shortcut is a practical follow-up for recorded wrong answers. Pair it with learning material when the method remains unclear. These reports describe your saved practice history; they do not generate official cutoffs, ranks or guaranteed readiness for an upcoming exam. Missing history should first be investigated as a selection, account or restore issue.

tasks.title: Use learning chapters alongside timed practice
tasks.body:
# Use learning chapters alongside timed practice

Learn provides topic material selected for the active exam. The AP and NICL chapter collections are separate, so confirm the exam context before looking for a particular chapter. Use the explanations to build a method, then test that method in a suitable practice session.

Sources attached to study topics are references, not a promise that every linked page is permanently available or that every fact remains current. Recruitment rules and current-affairs facts require fresh primary-source checks when updating content.

When adding a chapter, keep its topic identity consistent with the question bank and the exam selector. A polished heading does not establish syllabus coverage. Review the source list and test that the chapter is reachable through the intended exam and stage. Keep explanatory prose distinct from claims about original historical question papers.

tasks.title: Validate editorial question and archive changes
tasks.body:
# Validate editorial question and archive changes

Questions and historical-paper metadata need different checks. After editing the bank, run the bank validator and unit tests. After changing an archive source or key, run the paper validator as well. A TypeScript build alone does not establish that an answer is correct or that a PDF is an original booklet.

Use the existing commands from the repository root:

```bash
npm run validate:bank
npm run validate:papers
npm test
npm run build
```

Review the explanation, option ordering, answer index, exam identity and duplicated question families. For paper keys, verify the booklet-specific source and any amendments before changing a scored attempt. Browser tests cover interaction and timer behavior, while editorial review establishes content quality. Preserve that distinction in release notes and future source claims.

tasks.title: Recognise the severe AP SI question bank
tasks.body:
# Recognise the severe AP SI question bank

Version 2.1.0 added a severe bank of Hard AP SI practice items. Their ids begin with `sv`, and every item built through the shared helper is labelled Hard, carries a 120-second default allowance and shows the same source line: original severe practice, editorially authored and modelled on hard-question styles from recent recruitment exams.

Treat these items as practice, not as historical questions. Arithmetic and reasoning items are generated in code with computed answers, and arrangement puzzles are solved by brute force so that only one arrangement fits. General Studies and AP Focus items are hand-written in multi-statement, match-the-list, chronological ordering and assertion-reason formats.

Read the full explanation and hint after each attempt. A multi-statement question can be missed because of one statement, so check which statement caused the error before marking the whole topic as weak. Use the previous-paper archive when you need original booklets.

tasks.title: Understand how AP SI sets choose their difficulty mix
tasks.body:
# Understand how AP SI sets choose their difficulty mix

AP SI papers and AP practice sets use a dedicated selection policy. It targets 85% Hard, 12% Medium and the rest Easy, and within the Hard share it first reserves 85% for preferred items whose ids begin with `sv`, the severe bank. Remaining Hard places are filled from the other Hard items. NICL keeps the original default mix of 60% Hard, 30% Medium and 10% Easy.

The mix is applied after your filters. When Custom practice is limited to one difficulty, only that difficulty is eligible, so a Medium set stays Medium. If too few unique questions match, the app reports how many it needed and how many it found instead of padding the set with repeats.

Selection is seeded. The same seed and pool give the same set, which is why a paper can be rebuilt consistently. Expect AP sets to feel harder than earlier releases; compare scores across versions with care.

## Implementation references

- [src/lib/examEngine.ts](../../src/lib/examEngine.ts)

tasks.title: Know why repeated question patterns are capped in AP sets
tasks.body:
# Know why repeated question patterns are capped in AP sets

Older parts of the AP bank include parameterised templates: one sentence pattern with different numbers. To stop a single pattern recurring in one set, the AP policy groups questions into families by id and caps each family. Numeric `gqa-` and `gqr-` families allow one item per set. Knowledge-factory `xgs` and `xap` items allow two per frame and one per fact, and severe arithmetic frames allow two per set.

The caps are soft. When a small pool cannot fill the requested count, for example a saved-questions set made from one family, the capped items are added back so the session still starts with every requested question.

Caps only influence which items are drawn; ids are never changed. When you add a new templated family, give it an id pattern the family function can recognise, or add a pattern for it. The severe test checks that no AP paper exceeds any family cap across several seeds.

tasks.title: Interpret the Medium label on older numeric templates
tasks.body:
# Interpret the Medium label on older numeric templates

Before 2.1.0 the generated quant and reasoning templates, ids beginning `gqa-` and `gqr-`, marked some variants Hard by position alone. When the bank is assembled, any of those items labelled Hard is now relabelled Medium. Their ids, wording, options and answers are untouched.

This matters in two places. A Hard filter in Custom practice now draws on harder items instead of number-swapped templates, and AP papers no longer count these templates towards their Hard share. If a saved question or mistake you remember as Hard now shows Medium, the label changed, not the question.

Saved questions, mistakes and past attempts keep resolving because they are stored by id. Maintainers should keep that contract: correct labels at assembly time rather than renaming or rewriting existing items. The bank validator rejects any numeric template labelled Hard, and a test confirms that the old items still match their earlier text and answers.

tasks.title: Author new severe items with the shared severe kit
tasks.body:
# Author new severe items with the shared severe kit

New severe items should be built with the helpers in the severe kit rather than as hand-assembled objects. The `severe()` constructor rejects ids that do not start with `sv`, requires exactly four options and a whole-number answer index from 0 to 3, then fixes the difficulty to Hard and attaches the shared source line.

For options, `options4` places the correct answer at a seeded position among three distinct traps and throws when the traps collapse into duplicates. `numeric4` formats numeric traps with the same renderer and drops non-finite values. The kit's random generator is deterministic, so the bank is identical on every build.

Check `assemblyKey` for collisions. The bank is de-duplicated on letters and digits only, so two questions that differ only in symbols would be merged and one silently dropped. Then run the bank validator and the severe-bank tests before review.

tasks.title: Read the severe-bank checks in the bank validator
tasks.body:
# Read the severe-bank checks in the bank validator

`npm run validate:bank` includes checks dedicated to the severe bank. It requires at least 400 severe Arithmetic, 400 Reasoning, 250 General Studies and 150 AP Focus items. It rejects a subject whose answer key is unbalanced, meaning any option position holds less than 15% of that subject's answers.

Every severe item must be Hard, and the validator searches the question, options and explanation for rendering artefacts such as `NaN`, `undefined`, `Infinity` or `[object`. Those strings usually mean a generator interpolated a missing value.

On success it prints the total number of unique questions and, for each subject, the total, Hard and severe counts. Compare those counts with the previous run after a content change: a sudden fall in the severe count often means items were removed by de-duplication. Fix the generator or the wording; do not lower the minimums to make a failing run pass.

tasks.title: Run the severe-bank tests and the NICL fingerprint
tasks.body:
# Run the severe-bank tests and the NICL fingerprint

The severe-bank test file guards both content and selection. It confirms that every severe item reaches the assembled bank, that each has four distinct options, one valid answer and a real explanation and hint, and that answer positions in each subject fall between 15% and 35%. Every reasoning puzzle is re-solved and must have exactly one solution matching its key.

Selection tests build AP papers for several seeds and require at least 84% Hard and 70% severe items, at most 15% legacy templates, and no family above its cap.

The final test is a fingerprint. It builds NICL papers and practice sets for fixed seeds and compares a SHA-256 digest of the selected ids with a recorded value, proving the AP change did not alter NICL selection. If it fails, find the cause before updating the digest; never update it just to make the run pass. Run the suite with `npm test`.

tasks.title: Use the daily challenge as a short timed check
tasks.body:
# Use the daily challenge as a short timed check

The Study desk offers a daily challenge: ten questions with a 12-minute limit for the active exam, built from the same bank as Custom practice. For NICL, the selected stream decides whether IT Professional Knowledge questions are included. AP challenges follow the AP selection policy, so most items are Hard.

The set is seeded with the current date, so starting it again on the same day draws the same questions instead of a fresh set. Use a repeat as a check on what you corrected, not as new evidence of improvement. The date is read in UTC, so in India the set changes at 5:30 am rather than at midnight.

Only one test can be in progress. If a saved test is waiting, resume or submit it first; the challenge will not start over it. A completed challenge is saved as a practice attempt and appears in Performance.

tasks.title: Set your name, personal target date and daily study target
tasks.body:
# Set your name, personal target date and daily study target

Open **Profile & backup** from the sidebar or the avatar button to edit your profile. Your name is used in the Study desk greeting, and its first letter appears on the avatar button.

The personal target date is a planning date you choose. The dialog states that it is not an official exam date; always confirm schedules with the recruiting authority. The daily study target is in minutes and is kept between 15 and 1440, both when you type it and when a stored or imported profile is loaded. A new profile starts at 120 minutes.

These values belong to the profile, so they are included in exported backups and replaced when you import one. The Study desk's minutes figure is calculated from the time recorded in your attempts, not from the target you set. Keep the target realistic and compare it with recorded attempt time.

tasks.title: Open a specific exam view with a page link
tasks.body:
# Open a specific exam view with a page link

The address bar records where you are. After each change of exam, page, stage or NICL stream, the app rewrites the query string with `exam`, `view` and `stage`, and with `stream` for NICL only. It also sets the browser tab title from the page label and exam name, ending with Exam Prep King.

Open a link such as `?exam=nicl-ao&view=tests&stage=mains&stream=it` to land on NICL Mains in the Test series for the IT stream. Unknown values fall back safely: an unrecognised view opens the Study desk, any stage other than `mains` opens Prelims, and any stream other than `it` opens Generalist.

Links carry only the location, never progress. Your attempts and saved questions still come from this device or your account, so a link shared with someone else opens the same page with their own history. Rewriting uses history replacement, so changing pages does not add entries to the browser's back history.

tasks.title: Use keyboard, reduced-motion and contrast support
tasks.body:
# Use keyboard, reduced-motion and contrast support

Each page starts with a **Skip to content** link that moves keyboard focus past the sidebar to the main content. The navigation marks the current page for screen readers, and buttons that show only an icon, such as the menu, avatar and dismiss controls, carry descriptive labels.

Dialogs, including Profile & backup and the mobile navigation, use the native modal dialog. Escape closes them, the page behind stops scrolling while one is open, and every dialog has a labelled close button.

The interface respects system preferences. With reduced motion requested, animations and transitions are turned off and smooth scrolling is disabled. In forced-colours or high-contrast modes, buttons and links use system colours. Maintainers should keep these guarantees: the browser suite runs axe checks against WCAG 2.1 AA tags, including a mobile run with reduced motion, and expects no violations.

tasks.title: Build the Android app and keep its sign-in callback working
tasks.body:
# Build the Android app and keep its sign-in callback working

The Android app wraps the built web app with Capacitor. The configuration uses the app id `com.tpavan.lakshya`, the display name Exam Prep King and the `dist` folder as its web directory. `npm run android:sync` builds the web app and syncs it into the Android project; `npm run android:apk` also runs the Gradle debug build.

Sign-in works differently on the device. Inside the native app, Google sign-in opens in the system browser instead of redirecting the app's own page, and both Google and email sign-in return to `com.tpavan.lakshya://login-callback`. The app reads that link at launch or when it is opened, completes the session and closes the browser.

Changing the app id therefore also means changing the callback scheme and the allowed redirect settings for sign-in. When releasing, update the version in `package.json`, the Android `versionName`, a higher `versionCode` and the sidebar version label together.
